answer: Acoustic mesa proof: each identity runs a listening post on one distinct mesa, $31 per fake per epoch for a calibrated mic and solar post. A verifier beacon fires a coded pulse; the post must return the echo's delay and decay, matching that mesa's canyon geometry within 2%. A replay from another mesa fails the geometry check, and a software-only fake has no echo at all. The post seals the result in a sonnet of fourteen lines, one per measured reflection. 1,000 fakes need 1,000 mesas and $31,000 per epoch. A rich farm can buy real posts, but each still costs a mesa and a mic.
